:::: {.columns .faust-layout}

  - *Ramps* are often used as ***cursors*** to *read* or *write samples* in a ***buffer***. In Faust, *buffers* are implemented with the `rdtable` & `rwtable` primitives.
  - To playback a ***sound file***, we also typically use a phasor as a *read cursor*. 
:::
  - **Delaying** a signal in Faust can be done using the operator '**`@`**'. Thus, the expression *`x @ n`* delays a signal '`x`' by '`n`' **samples**.

::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}

  - *Ramps* are often used as ***cursors*** to *read* or *write samples* in a ***buffer***. In Faust, *buffers* are implemented with the `rdtable` & `rwtable` primitives.
  - To playback a ***sound file***, we also typically use a phasor as a *read cursor*. 
  - **Delaying** a signal in Faust can be done using the operator '**`@`**'. Thus, the expression *`x @ n`* delays a signal 'x' by 'n' **samples**.
:::
  - ***Delay times*** can usually be changed in real time from **GUI**, but it will in this case introduce unwanted '*clicks*'. We also here define a '***Dry/Wet***' control.
:::

<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->
## Faust: Buffers & Delays {auto-animate=true}
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

:::: {.columns .faust-layout}
::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}
::: {style="font-size: 85%;"}
::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
  - *Ramps* are often used as ***cursors*** to *read* or *write samples* in a ***buffer***. In Faust, *buffers* are implemented with the `rdtable` & `rwtable` primitives.
  - To playback a ***sound file***, we also typically use a phasor as a *read cursor*. 
  - **Delaying** a signal in Faust can be done using the operator '**`@`**'. Thus, the expression *`x @ n`* delays a signal 'x' by 'n' **samples**.
  - ***Delay times*** can usually be changed in real time from **GUI**, but it will in this case introduce unwanted '*clicks*'. We also here define a '***Dry/Wet***' control.
:::
  - Another typical control parameter for delays is the '***feedback coefficient***', which allows the delay to *repeat itself a certain number of times* before fading away. This will require to ***use the recursive operator***.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
```{.js code-line-numbers="20-21|24-26|" filename="faust/examples/time/delays-feedback.dsp"}
{{< include /faust/examples/time/delays-feedback.dsp >}}
```
{{< faust faust/examples/time/delays-feedback.dsp >}}
:::
::::
